findings.message: This regression is pinned to the wrong commodity: every origin stockpile is set to MIN_STOCK, so simulate_ai_trade picks the first key (fuel_cells), while `commodity` is the original maximum (microchips). The old minting path would add four fuel_cells and this assertion would still pass because microchips never move. Assert conservation for every commodity, or pick the same key the trader will pic

The floor fix still lets a trade destroy goods at the destination: _adjust_stock clamps target stock at MAX_STOCK, so when the target is full the moved quantity disappears. The commit's conservation promise is only half kept. Limit the move by the destination headroom as well and add a ceiling regression next to the floor test; because that changes deterministic trade amounts, verify the campaign-

A 200 response with malformed JSON is returned as status 200 with ok=false, so AiCaptain.play records it as a refusal and still counts the endpoint as attempted; coverage_gaps and report.ok can both pass while the endpoint is broken. Return a non-200/protocol status so play appends an error instead of a refusal.

The new transit lock is checked by scan, land, salvage and scoop, but trade and refuel still succeed mid-flight because start_travel leaves ship.orbiting_body_id at the origin station. A player can launch and keep trading or refuelling at the station they just left. Apply the transit guard to every station service, or clear orbiting_body_id on departure while keeping origin_body_id for the abort p
findings.evidence: """Body actions need a real orbit; mid-flight the ship has left the old body."""

        origin = replace(origin, stockpiles={cid: MIN_STOCK for cid in origin.stockpiles})
        markets["sol"] = origin
        economy = replace(engine.state.economy, markets=markets)
        before = sum(m.stockpiles.get(commodity, 0) for m in markets.values())

        )
        after = sum(m.stockpiles.get(commodity, 0) for m in updated_economy.markets.values())

findings.message: The legacy backfill runs on every load and recomputes every body's tech/capacity from the static faction tier. A world that tech drift raised above that tier is downgraded on the next load: a Sol desert world at TL10 with 1.34B capacity reloads at TL9 with 1.03B. Limit the static recompute to bodies with no capacity field so drifted and conquered technology survives save/load.
